headline: The US–Iran war keeps Hormuz largely shut after tankers were hit on 5 Nov; Russia–Ukraine and the Middle East stay at Alert, and Bundibugyo Ebola in DR Congo has passed 10,000 cases.

situations.name: US–Iran war and Gulf energy shock
situations.summary: Tankers hit in Hormuz on 5 Nov; Tehran contacts Gulf states amid fears of US strikes. Brent rebounds to about $97.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine war and NATO's flank
situations.summary: Russian strikes keep hitting Ukraine's grid; an aid-centre strike on 3 Nov was among the deadliest. Talks set for 10–11 Nov.

situations.name: Super El Niño
situations.summary: ONI rose to +2.5 for Aug–Oct: drought risk in East and southern Africa, record-range warmth and faster CO₂ growth.

situations.name: Ebola outbreak, DR Congo
situations.summary: ECDC counted 10,274 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,992 deaths in DR Congo to 28 Oct; imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria; a WHO PHEIC since May.

situations.name: Sudan war
situations.summary: UN warns of deadly drone strikes on Sudan's grid and civilians; a South Kordofan fuel-station strike killed at least 7 on 4 Nov.

situations.name: France: debt stress and protests
situations.summary: OAT–Bund spread near 160bp; nationwide strike on 5 Nov with largely peaceful marches; budget deadline 17 Nov.

situations.name: Energy shock feeding inflation
situations.summary: Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov and warned inflation will near 5%; US CPI 4.0%; RBA hiked on 3 Nov.

situations.name: Binance theft and North Korean escalation
situations.summary: FBI blames North Korea for a $6.3bn Binance theft; Pyongyang denied it and fired several missiles on 4 Nov. Binance withdrawals have resumed.

signals.name: US equity stress
signals.summary: S&P 500 falls over 3% on 5 Nov as chip stocks slide; drawdown passes the 5% Watch line
signals.state: The S&P 500 fell more than 3% on 5 Nov, its worst day since 2025, and the Nasdaq dropped about 5% as AI and chip stocks sold off, erasing the post-midterm rally (Yahoo Finance; BNN Bloomberg). The index is 5.3% below its 52-week high and the VIX rose to about 24.5, both inside the Watch band. October payrolls on 6 Nov are the next test.
signals.for_you: Market falls feed through to pensions and investment funds with equity exposure; this describes conditions, not a reason to act.
signals.rubric_hit: VIX 28.2 ≥ 20 Watch line; S&P drawdown 5.95% ≥ 5% Watch line

signals.name: FTSE 100
signals.summary: FTSE 100 near 10,829, 0.8% below its high; no large daily falls this week
signals.state: The FTSE 100 closed near 10,829 on 4 Nov, 0.8% below its 52-week high and 1.0% higher on the week; its worst day in the past five sessions was a 1.1% fall (Yahoo Finance). That is well inside the 5% drawdown and 2.5% daily-fall Watch lines. The Bank of England announces its rate decision on 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: UK shares are near record levels. Pension and ISA holders in UK equities face normal market swings; nothing indicates stress as of 5 Nov.
signals.rubric_hit: FTSE drawdown 1.17% below the 5% Watch line

signals.name: Bond market volatility
signals.summary: Treasury volatility eases to MOVE 94; 10-year yield 4.89%, about 38bp lower on the month
signals.state: The MOVE index of Treasury volatility was about 94 on 4 Nov, down from about 100 on 3 Nov, and the US 10-year yield was 4.89%, about 38bp lower than a month earlier (Yahoo Finance). Both readings sit just under the Watch lines (MOVE 100, 40bp a month), so Watch is kept until they clear them. October payrolls on 6 Nov are the next test.
signals.for_you: Bond markets remain more volatile than usual. Mortgage and loan pricing can move quickly while yields swing around data releases and central-bank decisions.
signals.rubric_hit: MOVE 97.9 has not yet cleared the 90 exit line, so Watch holds; US10y 1m move 39.4bp has not yet cleared the 36bp exit line, so Watch holds

signals.name: Credit spreads
signals.summary: US high-yield spreads 3.40%, inside the 4% Watch line
signals.state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.40% on 3 Nov, inside the 4% Watch line, about 28bp wider than a month earlier and near its widest in a year (FRED). There is no sign of a broad credit squeeze as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Borrowing conditions for riskier companies remain open. Wider spreads would mean costlier credit for indebted firms; that is not happening as of 5 Nov.
signals.rubric_hit: HY OAS 3.32% below the 4% Watch line

signals.name: US dollar
signals.summary: Dollar index near 101.2, up 1.4% over three months
signals.state: The DXY dollar index was near 101.2 early on 5 Nov, up 1.4% over three months and 0.6% lower on the week (Yahoo Finance), well inside the 5% Watch line and the 90–108 range. No dollar funding strain is visible.
signals.for_you: Exchange rates against the dollar are steady. Travellers and importers face normal currency movements as of 5 Nov.

signals.name: Banking system stress
signals.summary: Financial stress gauges low; no bank failures reported
signals.state: The St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index was −0.52 in the week to 30 Oct, below its long-run average, and the ECB's systemic stress indicator was 0.0078 on 3 Nov, far below the 0.25 Watch line. No US or European bank failure or rescue had been reported as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Banking systems show no stress. Deposit protection schemes such as the UK FSCS apply as normal.
signals.rubric_hit: STLFSI -0.52 below the 0 Watch line; ECB CISS 0.01 below the 0.25 Watch line

signals.name: Gold (fear gauge)
signals.summary: Gold near $4,128, up 5.9% on the week but 6.6% lower over three months
signals.state: Gold futures were near $4,128 early on 5 Nov, 6.6% lower over three months, inside the Normal band of −8% to +10% (Yahoo Finance). The price rose 5.9% over the past week, below the 7% single-week Alert line, and remains about 22% under its 52-week high.
signals.for_you: Gold has rebounded but is not signalling a flight to safety. Its price can move sharply with interest-rate expectations.

signals.name: Crypto stress
signals.summary: Bitcoin near $80,500, 7% off its high; no stablecoin de-peg
signals.state: Bitcoin was near $80,500 early on 5 Nov, 7% below its 52-week high and up 3.9% on the week, far from the 25% Watch line (Yahoo Finance). Binance withdrawals resumed from 1 Nov after the theft the FBI attributes to North Korea, and no stablecoin de-peg or exchange failure had been reported as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Crypto prices are steady by their own standards. Holders on exchanges remain exposed to hacks and withdrawal freezes, which are not covered by deposit protection.

signals.summary: SOFR peaked 7bp above the reserve rate; Fed repo use near zero
signals.state: SOFR peaked 7bp above the Fed's interest on reserves in the five days to 3 Nov, inside the 10bp Watch line, and Fed overnight repo operations were near zero to 4 Nov (FRED). Money markets show no sign of a dollar shortage as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Short-term dollar funding markets are working normally.
signals.rubric_hit: SOFR–IORB 5d max 7bp below the 10bp Watch line; Fed repo ops 5d max $0bn below the $15bn Watch line

signals.name: Private credit stress
signals.summary: Non-traded BDC redemption requests still exceed quarterly caps; no forced sales or bank spillover
signals.state: Redemption requests at non-traded BDCs, including Blackstone's BCRED, have run well above the usual 5% quarterly caps, and requests now exceed new fundraising (InvestmentNews; Bloomberg Government). Gates remain in force at several funds. No forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers had been reported as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may face limits on withdrawals; borrowers reliant on private lenders may find credit tighter.
signals.rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions = Watch; no multi-fund gating with forced sales

signals.state: The dollar was near ¥157.9 early on 5 Nov, up 0.1% on the week and down 0.1% on the month, far inside the 3% weekly and 6% monthly Watch lines (Yahoo Finance). No Japanese currency intervention had been reported as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: The yen is stable. Travellers to Japan and firms trading in yen face normal exchange-rate movements.

signals.summary: Sahm indicator 0.00; yield curve +0.32; October payrolls due 6 Nov
signals.state: The real-time Sahm rule indicator is 0.00 (September data), far from the 0.5 trigger, and the 10y–2y Treasury curve was +0.32 on 4 Nov (FRED). October payrolls are due on 6 Nov.
signals.for_you: US labour-market data show no recession signal. Firms and workers exposed to the US economy face normal conditions as of 5 Nov.

signals.name: US inflation
signals.summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September; October data due 10 Nov
signals.state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7%, inside the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). Brent rebounded on 5 Nov from a two-month low near $94 as uncertainty over the Iran war persisted (The National), so energy prices remain a risk to the October figure, due on 10 Nov.
signals.for_you: Higher prices for fuel, food and services squeeze household budgets; mortgage and loan rates tend to stay high while inflation is above target.
signals.rubric_hit: CPI 4.0% within 3.0–4.5% Watch band

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.summary: Euro-area composite PMI 51.9 in October; Q3 GDP grew 0.4%
signals.state: The HCOB euro-area flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 in October, below the 52.7 expected but above 50 (FXStreet, 23 Oct). Eurostat's flash estimate showed Q3 GDP up 0.4%. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI had been reported as of 5 Nov, so the Normal criteria still hold.
signals.for_you: Euro-area growth is positive but slowing; exporters and jobs in energy-heavy industries remain most exposed.
signals.rubric_hit: GDP +0.4% and composite PMI 51.9 > 50 = Normal

signals.name: China economy
signals.summary: China services growth slows to 50.8 in October; factory PMI in contraction
signals.state: China's Caixin services PMI eased to 50.8 in October, a three-month low, as confidence weakened (Yahoo Finance; investingLive, 4 Nov). The official manufacturing PMI was 49.3 and regulators paused IPOs to steady stocks in early November. Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Slower Chinese demand weighs on commodity exporters and firms selling into China; no acute disruption is reported.
signals.rubric_hit: Growth near target, no contagion = Normal

signals.name: Central bank stress
signals.summary: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov and warns inflation will near 5%
signals.state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, and warned inflation will approach 5% as the energy shock feeds through (CNBC; Bank of England). Australia's central bank hiked to 4.85% on 3 Nov, and the ECB and Bank of Japan held in late October. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move has been made.
signals.for_you: Borrowing costs are rising again in several economies; variable-rate mortgages and new loans are most exposed.
signals.rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma at major central banks = Watch; no emergency moves

signals.name: Sovereign debt stress
signals.summary: France–Bund spread near 160bp, above the 150bp Alert line, as unions strike on 5 Nov
signals.state: France's 10-year spread over German Bunds was reported near 160bp in the week to 5 Nov, above the 150bp Alert line, as the 2027 budget vote slipped toward a 17 Nov deadline (Journal du Coin; Trading Economics). Unions held a nationwide strike on 5 Nov (Al Jazeera). No failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying has been reported.
signals.for_you: Higher French borrowing costs can feed through to euro-area mortgage and corporate rates; this describes market conditions only.
signals.rubric_hit: France–Bund ~160bp > 150bp Alert line

signals.summary: Global manufacturing PMI 52.6 in October; composite reading still above 51 in latest data
signals.state: The J.P.Morgan Global Manufacturing PMI eased to 52.6 in October from 53.0, still well above 50 (S&P Global). The global composite was at its joint-highest since 2021 in September; the October composite had not been found as of 5 Nov. No reading near the 51 Watch line has been reported.
signals.for_you: Global factory activity is still expanding; no broad downturn is signalled for trade-exposed jobs.

signals.summary: US jobless claims 4-week average 195k, at its 52-week low
signals.state: Initial US jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 31 Oct, pulling the four-week average down to about 194,750, its 52-week low and far from the 15% Watch line (Department of Labor via FRED). Layoffs remain low as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Layoffs remain low, so job security for most US workers is not under new pressure.
signals.rubric_hit: 4wk avg 0% above 52w low < 15% = Normal

signals.name: Emerging-market stress
signals.value: Lira past 50/$; EGP at record low
signals.summary: Turkish lira breaches 50 per dollar; no major EM default or capital controls
signals.state: The Turkish lira broke through 50 per dollar to a record low on 4 Nov, extending a gradual slide (Shafaq News; Trading Economics). Egypt's pound has also hit record lows. Neither has lost more than 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF help as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Weaker currencies raise import costs in Turkey and Egypt; travellers and exporters see changing exchange rates.
signals.rubric_hit: No major EM >10% monthly fall, default or controls = Normal

signals.state: Brent rebounded on 5 Nov to about $97 from a two-month low as uncertainty over the Iran war lingered (The National), a price in the Watch band and down 7% in a month. Alert is kept on the physical outage: Hormuz remains largely shut and more tankers were hit in the strait on 5 Nov (US News).
signals.for_you: Fuel and heating costs stay exposed to Gulf supply news; prices can swing sharply on reports from the talks.
signals.rubric_hit: Brent $99.4 has not yet cleared the $99 exit line, so Alert holds

signals.state: Dutch TTF gas closed near €85/MWh on 4 Nov, 14% lower on the week on hopes for US–Iran talks but still above the €70 Alert line and 53% higher over three months (Yahoo Finance). Hormuz, the route for Qatari LNG, remained largely shut, with the IRGC claiming mine strikes on tankers south of the strait on 4 Nov (Al Jazeera).
signals.for_you: Wholesale gas prices feed into household energy bills and industrial costs with a lag. In the UK, Ofgem's price cap sets what most households pay.

signals.summary: More tankers hit in Hormuz on 5 Nov as Iran keeps pressure on after the US vote
signals.state: Tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on 5 Nov as Iran kept up pressure after the US midterms, a day after IRGC claims of mine strikes south of the strait (US News; CBS News). Iran ties reopening the strait to an end to the US naval blockade. Traffic remains materially impeded, meeting the Alert line.
signals.for_you: Shipping delays and higher insurance costs feed into fuel and goods prices; follow FCDO travel advice for the Gulf region.

signals.state: The FAO Food Price Index rose to 136.0 in September, its highest since November 2022 and above the 135 Alert line, led by cereals and sugar (FAO; MercoPress, 8 Oct). FAO has scheduled its October update for 6 Nov; no new reading as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Food bills are likely to stay high, especially for staples and in import-dependent countries.

signals.summary: China's rare-earth export-control pause expires 10 Nov with no renewal announced
signals.state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls, including the 0.1% content rule, expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 5 Nov (Yahoo Finance; Technology.org). Lapsed controls would bring back tighter licensing. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed, so the Alert line is not crossed.
signals.for_you: Manufacturers of magnets, motors and electronics face licensing delays if controls return.

signals.summary: Gulf urea exports still stuck behind a largely closed Hormuz; tankers hit on 5 Nov
signals.state: Hormuz, a route for about a third of world urea exports, remains largely closed in the conflict's ninth month, keeping fertiliser costs high (Global Agriculture; European Commission). Tankers were hit in the strait again on 5 Nov (US News). A key export route closed meets the Alert line.
signals.for_you: Farmers face higher input costs, which can feed into food prices next season.
signals.rubric_hit: Key export route (Hormuz) closed = Alert

signals.name: Nuclear plant safety
signals.summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on a single power line as Russian strikes hit Ukraine's grid
signals.state: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has relied on a single off-site line since repairs agreed under an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire (Arms Control Association). Russian strikes continued to hit Ukraine's energy system into 5 Nov (Forbes). No damage to safety systems or radiological release has been reported.
signals.for_you: No public health action is advised; follow IAEA and national regulator updates.
signals.rubric_hit: Plant on minimal off-site power amid grid strikes = Watch

signals.name: US–China / Taiwan
signals.summary: Surge to 49 PLA aircraft around Taiwan on 3 Nov; no large-scale exercise announced
signals.state: Taiwan's defence ministry reported 49 Chinese military aircraft, six warships and six official ships around Taiwan in the 24 hours to 3 Nov, one of the busiest days this year (TaiwanPlus); reports also describe a large naval mobilisation (SCMP). China has not announced an exercise. China's pause on rare-earth export controls ends on 10 Nov. Normal holds until a declared large-scale drill or incident.
signals.for_you: No direct effect for most people as of 5 Nov. Firms reliant on Taiwanese chips or Taiwan Strait shipping are the most exposed if activity escalates.
signals.rubric_hit: No declared large-scale exercise, blockade or incident; activity elevated = Normal

signals.name: Russia–NATO
signals.summary: Russian nuclear warnings over Kaliningrad stand; no Article 4 request as of 5 Nov
signals.state: Russia warned NATO in late September, including in a formal diplomatic note, that it would use 'all means', including nuclear weapons, against any action on Kaliningrad; NATO's Mark Rutte called the threats unhelpful (Arms Control Association, Nov issue). Russia's mass strike on Ukraine on 3–4 Nov hit Kovel in Volyn, near the Polish border (The Defense Post). No NATO member had requested Article 4 consultations as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Travellers to eastern NATO states should follow FCDO travel advice. Airspace closures near the Ukrainian border can disrupt flights at short notice.
signals.rubric_hit: Explicit threats against members; no Article 4 or clash = Watch

signals.summary: No IAEA access to key Iranian sites; nuclear talks tied to Iran's war terms
signals.state: The IAEA has had no access to key Iranian sites and reported Iran to the UN Security Council in October (Arms Control Association). Iran's conditions for reopening Hormuz, rejected as unconvincing on 3 Nov, centre on sanctions relief and the US blockade; US strikes on 3 Nov hit an air-defence site on Qeshm Island, not nuclear facilities (Al Jazeera). No strike on a nuclear site had been reported as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: No direct effect for most people. Developments here can move oil prices and regional travel advice; follow FCDO guidance.

The launch followed Pyongyang's denial of US claims that it stole about $6.3bn from Binance. No nuclear test or ICBM overflight of Japan has been reported as of 5 Nov.

signals.name: Civil unrest
signals.summary: Nationwide strike in France on 5 Nov with largely peaceful marches; 70,000 police deployed
signals.state: Workers struck across France on 5 Nov, with hundreds of thousands expected to march over living costs and the budget (Al Jazeera; CNN). Marches were largely peaceful, and about 270,000 marched outside Paris by union counts (ThePrint; Rio Times). The government deployed about 70,000 police. signals.name: UK inflation & rates
signals.summary: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov; warns inflation will near 5%
signals.state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, reversing its easing cycle, and warned inflation will approach 5% (CNBC; Bank of England). UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band.
signals.for_you: Variable and tracker mortgages, and new fixed deals, are likely to cost more; savings rates may rise.

signals.name: Gilt market
signals.summary: Gilt yields rise after the Bank of England's first hike since 2023 on 5 Nov
signals.state: Gilt yields rose on 5 Nov after the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4%, its first rise in three years, with two-year gilts most affected (Euronext). The 10-year yield was near 5.2% in early November, below its mid-October multi-year high near 5.4% (Trading Economics). No weak auction or BoE intervention has been reported.

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.summary: Energy cap £1,723; final January forecasts point to the highest cap since January 2024
signals.state: The Ofgem cap for October–December is £1,723 a year. Cornwall Insight has released its final January forecast, and reports say the cap will rise to its highest since January 2024; its earlier forecast was £1,999, up 16% (Cornwall Insight; Hargreaves Lansdown). signals.for_you: Households on standard variable tariffs should expect higher bills from January; Ofgem and Citizens Advice list support schemes.
